subject.title: [Refactor] Abstract OAuth flow parameters out of LLM transport core

question: Should remaining LLM OAuth transport parameters use existing provider-plugin hooks, or should `@openclaw/ai` gain a new public OAuth configuration contract?
rationale: Both boundaries are plausible, but a new contract would become compatibility-sensitive API surface and the issue does not establish that current provider hooks cannot carry the required data.

options.title: Use Provider Hooks
options.body: Extend existing provider-owned auth and transport-normalization hooks only for the concrete missing parameters, preserving one ownership path.

options.title: Add AI Contract
options.body: Create a reviewed `@openclaw/ai` OAuth contract only if library consumers require provider-neutral OAuth injection independent of OpenClaw plugins.

options.title: Keep Current Boundary
options.body: Decline the refactor if inspection shows the remaining literals are intentional built-in transport protocol constants rather than provider policy.

recommendation.title: Use Provider Hooks
recommendation.body: Extend existing provider-owned auth and transport-normalization hooks only for the concrete missing parameters, preserving one ownership path.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice concerns the repository-wide lean-core and provider-ownership boundary reflected in current architecture policy.
